correctness.rationale: The published H-description consists of nonnegativity facets and maximal-chain facets. A radius-\(\rho\) ball forces every coordinate to be at least \(\rho\); applying a longest-chain facet of normal norm \(\sqrt h\) gives the sharp upper bound \(\rho\le1/(h+\sqrt h)\). The uniform point \(r\mathbf1\) meets every shorter chain with at least the same clearance because \(k+\sqrt k\) is increasing. The complete center set follows from the same normalized clearances. Longest-chain saturation proves uniqueness when longest chains cover the poset, and an explicit positive perturbation gives nonuniqueness otherwise.

value.rationale: Chain polytopes are one of the canonical poset-polytope constructions and occur as extremal members of modern marked-poset families. The theorem gives a complete all-poset Euclidean inradius law controlled by the most basic order statistic, height, while showing that center uniqueness detects strictly finer structure: coverage by longest chains. This clean separation between radius and center-set complexity is a natural metric complement to the established Ehrhart and face-structure theory.
